# Programs whose result rax-user does not reproduce yet, per execution mode.
# The test requires each listed program to still differ and every other
# program to match (see the README).
#
#   mode  program  cause
#
# mode: x86_64, x86_64-nojit, aarch64, riscv64, or riscv64-jit.
x86_64 02_fibonacci x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64 06_allocator x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64 08_json_parser x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64 10_template_madness x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64-nojit 02_fibonacci x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64-nojit 06_allocator x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64-nojit 08_json_parser x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
x86_64-nojit 10_template_madness x87 registers are held as binary64 in the direct engine (FpuState.st), so musl printf, which formats through long double, rounds the last digit wrongly
